undefined-strict-policy.resolution: The ratified named profile rejects this undefined spelling. Native extensions/acceptance/error-detection choices neither weaken the profile nor establish universal POSIX invalidity.

unspecified-strict-policy.resolution: The ratified strict disposition selects rejection where Issue7 leaves behavior unspecified. Native acceptance or another symbolic category is recorded, not a product golden result.

normative-subpattern-priority.clause: XBD9.1 left-to-right longest subpatterns consistent with whole
normative-subpattern-priority.resolution: Keep the normative longest preceding subpattern; glibc final registers select the shorter left alternative. Native source set_regs/proceed_next_node recovers one admissible path; it is not the contract priority reference.

normative-report-parent-scope.clause: XSH regexec nested subexpression in last containing match
normative-report-parent-scope.resolution: Keep nested group absent if absent in the last reported parent iteration. glibc retains an earlier nested register; regexec.c update_regs refreshes visited group slots without clearing all absent descendants.

normative-reference-parent-scope.clause: XBD9.3.6 contained backreference within last containing match
normative-reference-parent-scope.resolution: NoMatch remains mandatory even when both native families disagree. In abab, the purported final reference needs b from outside its final containing match; an unparticipated reference cannot fabricate the empty acceptance musl reports. Reduced exact pattern/subject and both observations retained.

normative-unmatched-reference.resolution: NoMatch on a is stated by the source example. musl backreference computes eo-so=0 for absent(-1,-1) and strncmp length0 succeeds instead of rejecting absence.

normative-reference-case.resolution: REG_ICASE applies to reference equality. musl backreference path regexec.c uses raw strncmp without counterpart comparison; preserve Match and full byte endpoints under the frozen ASCII provider.

native-singleton-collation-gap.resolution: Singleton symbols and singleton primary equivalence remain admitted. musl regcomp.c parse_bracket_terms explicitly returns REG_ECOLLATE for both constructs. This is an oracle capability gap, not an approved GregsEx exclusion.

provider-high-byte-disposition.resolution: Raw high-byte singleton collation is the ratified named-provider choice. musl does not implement this bracket syntax. No portable C codeset or unrestricted locale claim is made.
